messages.subject: tlengh argument of gdistsamp
parts:
Greetings all,

I'am using gdistsamp function with line transect method to predict the distribution of large mobile birds. There are 10 replicates and 40 sites. Each site is composed of 1 transect (4000m) thus where we repeat survey 10 times. Is the "tlength" argument the transect length or the total sampling effort i.e. transect length x number of replicates ?

Thanks,

Thomas DENIS

Doctorant UAG / ECOFOG

messages.subject: Re: tlengh argument of gdistsamp
parts:
Hi Richard,

Thanks a lot for the answer!

But I certainly have a problem with the implementation of the gdistsamp function. I have asked the previous question because I have outlier results. The estimated densities per site are very high (x10) compared to what I have expected from previous analysis. When I used classical distance sampling (distsamp function), the outcomes varied from 2 to 7 animals/km². Furthermore, I read (Chandler et al, 2011) that densities are over-estimated when the animal's home range is large and thus the temporary emigration is not taken into account.

We have sampled each site  for 10 consecutive half-days (10 replicates). Thus, we have walked 4000m (transect length) per half-day. Each site have a sampling effort of 40000m. Firstly, I wrote the following script:

umf <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y = y, siteCovs=ttG1, survey="line", unitsIn="m", dist.breaks=seq(0, 50, by=5), tlength=rep(4000, 40), numPrimary=T)

where y is the observations matrix with 40 rows and 10 distance intervals x 10 replicates=100 columns (the 10 first columns are the number of individual per distance intervals for the first replicate, the 10 following columns [...] for the second replicate, etc), ttG1 is the covariates dataframe with 40 rows (sites), the number of sites, T=10 is the number of replicates.

Secondly,

lDsModel <- list()
lDsModel$PM<-gdistsamp(pentemoy+chasse,  ~1, ~1, umf, keyfun ="halfnorm",unitsOut = "kmsq",  output="density", mixture = "NB",K=50)
lDsModel$P<-gdistsamp(pentemoy,  ~1, ~1, umf, keyfun ="halfnorm",unitsOut = "kmsq",  output="density", mixture = "NB",K=50)
lDsModel$NULL<-gdistsamp(~1,  ~1, ~1, umf, keyfun ="halfnorm",unitsOut = "kmsq",  output="density", mixture = "NB",K=50)
lDsModel$PMH<-gdistsamp(pentemoy+chasse+HP1,  ~1, ~1, umf, keyfun ="halfnorm",unitsOut = "kmsq",  output="density", mixture = "NB",K=50)
...
...
...

where pentemoy, chasse, HP1, ... are the abundance covariates


Finally, I predicted estimated densities from models with a deltaAIC lower than 2 (AICcmodavg package)

modHoccAV<-modavgPred(lDsModel[1:5], newdata=umf@siteCovs, second.ord = FALSE,
                      type = "response", nobs = NULL,
                      uncond.se = "revised", parm.type = "lambda")


Please, where would the error come from?

Thomas

Thanks,

Thomas DENIS

Doctorant UAG / ECOFOG

A l’ONCFS - Direction Etudes et Recherche Guyane

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: tlengh argument of gdistsamp
parts:
Hi Thomas,

In our paper, we were making the point that density will be overestimated if you incorrectly assume closure (over multiple survey occasions) in the presence of temporary emigration. Your distsamp() analysis does not assume closure over multiple survey occasions so the estimates should be fine. 

When using gdistsamp(), lambda is the expected value of the super-population, E(M)=lambda. The expected value of abundance during occasion k is E(N) = lambda*phi.

Richard
